---
title: Ingestion
description: From sequencing to count tables
order: 20
---

Ingestion covers the steps that take raw sequencing output — BCL files from the sequencer or pre-converted FASTQ files — and produce per-sample count matrices stored as H5MU files. These H5MU files are the starting point for all downstream processing workflows.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-ingestion-overview
%%| fig-cap: Overview of the ingestion step, from raw sequencer output to an H5MU count matrix.
flowchart LR
  bcl["BCL files"] --> demux["Demultiplexing"]
  demux --> fastq["FASTQ files"]
  fastq --> mapping["Mapping & quantification"]
  mapping --> h5mu["H5MU (count matrix)"]
  ref["Reference genome"] --> mapping
```

## Reference genome

Before mapping, a reference genome index must be prepared. OpenPipelines provides the `make_reference` workflow, which builds a reference compatible with Cell Ranger:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/ingestion/make_reference/main.nf \
  -revision 4.0.3 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  --id GRCh38 \
  --genome_fasta Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.dna.primary_assembly.fa \
  --annotation_gtf Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.111.gtf \
  --output reference_genome/ \
  --publish_dir results/
```

Pre-built references from 10x Genomics can also be used directly with the mapping workflows.

## Demultiplexing (BCL → FASTQ)

If starting from raw BCL files, the `demux` workflow converts them to per-sample FASTQ files using `bcl2fastq` or `bcl_convert`:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/ingestion/demux/main.nf \
  -revision 4.0.3 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  --id run_001 \
  --input /path/to/bcl_run/ \
  --sample_sheet SampleSheet.csv \
  --output demux_output/ \
  --publish_dir results/
```

If your sequencing provider delivers FASTQ files directly, skip this step.

## Mapping and quantification

OpenPipelines provides dedicated ingestion workflows for the two most common platforms.

### 10x Genomics (Cell Ranger)

The `cellranger_mapping` workflow aligns FASTQ files and generates a feature-barcode count matrix:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/ingestion/cellranger_mapping/main.nf \
  -revision 4.0.3 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  --id sample_A \
  --input "fastq_dir/" \
  --reference reference_genome/ \
  --output sample_A.h5mu \
  --publish_dir results/
```

For multiomics experiments (GEX + VDJ + ADT/HTO from the same cell), use `cellranger_multi`, which handles multiple library types in a single Cell Ranger run:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/ingestion/cellranger_multi/main.nf \
  -revision 4.0.3 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  --id sample_A \
  --input "fastq_dir/" \
  --gex_reference reference_genome/ \
  --feature_reference feature_reference.csv \
  --output sample_A.h5mu \
  --publish_dir results/
```

### BD Rhapsody

For BD Rhapsody single-cell data, use the dedicated `bd_rhapsody` workflow:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/ingestion/bd_rhapsody/main.nf \
  -revision 4.0.3 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  --id sample_A \
  --input "fastq_dir/*.fastq.gz" \
  --reference reference.tar.gz \
  --output sample_A.h5mu \
  --publish_dir results/
```

## Format conversion

If you already have count matrices in another format, OpenPipelines provides converters to H5MU:

| Input format | Component |
|---|---|
| 10x HDF5 (`.h5`) | `convert/from_10xh5_to_h5mu` |
| 10x MEX (`.mtx` + barcodes + features) | `convert/from_10xmtx_to_h5mu` |
| BD Rhapsody output | `convert/from_bdrhap_to_h5mu` |
| AnnData H5AD | `convert/from_h5ad_to_h5mu` |
| Seurat RDS | `convert/from_seurat_to_h5mu` |

## Processing multiple samples at once

Use `--param_list` to run ingestion over multiple samples in one command. See the [Parameter lists](parameter_lists.qmd) page for details on the supported formats (CSV, YAML, JSON).

Example `params.csv`:

```
id,input,reference
sample_A,fastq/sample_A/,reference_genome/
sample_B,fastq/sample_B/,reference_genome/
sample_C,fastq/sample_C/,reference_genome/
```

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/ingestion/cellranger_mapping/main.nf \
  -revision 4.0.3 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  --param_list params.csv \
  --publish_dir results/
```

## Output

All ingestion workflows produce one H5MU file per sample. The H5MU file stores the count matrix in the `rna` modality (and additional modalities when applicable, e.g. `prot` for ADT, `vdj` for immune repertoire). This file is the input for the [processing workflows](processing.qmd).

See the [Components reference](../components/) for the full argument list of each ingestion workflow.
